title: Support QA (SUP), 24 Oct 2026
headline: 77 of 108 open support tickets look stuck, and 62 haven’t been touched in a month.
subhead: 31 are waiting on us with no update in 14+ days, and 19 of the 26 pending tickets have no linked delivery ticket, against the rule that parked work is linked. Time to resolution has already breached on 75 open tickets, so that SLA no longer separates stuck from slow.

checks.name: Stalled on us
checks.rule: Waiting for support with no update in 14+ days.

checks.name: No customer update in 30 days
checks.rule: Waiting for support or Pending, and no team comment in 30+ days.

checks.name: Pending, no link

checks.param: delivery links: any link to a non-SUP issue

checks.name: Linked work unscheduled

sections.title: Ready to resolve
sections.cap: All linked delivery work is done; close the loop with the requester.

sections.title: Stalled on us
sections.cap: Waiting for support with no update in 14+ days, or no team comment in 30+ days. Oldest update first.

sections.title: Customer gone quiet
sections.cap: Waiting for customer for 14+ days. Nudge once, then resolve per the auto-close policy. Longest wait first.

sections.title: Pending without a clear path
sections.cap: Pending, but missing a linked delivery ticket or a Pending reason, or the linked work is still unscheduled.

sections.title: Enhancements not routed
sections.cap: Enhancement requests older than 7 days that aren’t yet Pending and linked to a delivery board.

sections.title: Moving, or pending the right way

findings: It has breached on 75 of 108 open tickets, and it pauses while a ticket is Pending, so a ticket parked for months never trips it. That’s why it isn’t a QA check here.
Timely Updates measures time in Pending, not updates

Its clock starts when a ticket enters Pending and keeps running through comments, so the report computes “No customer update in 30 days” from the last team comment instead. 51 tickets have gone 30+ days without one. The connector doesn’t expose whether a comment was public or internal, so an internal note currently counts as an update.
Due dates don’t mean much yet
62 of the 72 tickets with a due date are past it. If due dates are set by automation at intake, this check mostly repeats the SLA.
Pending is where tickets go to wait
Median time in Pending is 216 days. 19 of 26 have no linked work and 14 have no Pending reason.
19 open tickets are enhancement requests; only 2 are Pending and linked.

Links to delivery boards use 6 types (Polaris work item link, Discovery - Connected, Relates, Blocks, Duplicate, and Polaris datapoint work item link). Standardizing on one would let the report trust the link’s meaning.
54 of 108 open tickets sit with Avery Caldwell, including 26 stalled on us.
spec: Same as the Product QA report: bands, hairlines, Lora and Mulish embedded as base64, dd MMM yyyy dates, one QA cell showing only failing glyphs, ledger and owner filters, and print rules. Both reports inline the shared stylesheet assets/qa_base.css.

An aging strip, not a target-date runway. Support tickets have no planned target, and how long it has been since anyone touched a ticket is the stuck signal. Tickets are bucketed by days since last update; the stale line and wash mark where slow becomes stuck.
Dot colors encode whose move it is
Dawn is us, Legacy is the customer, and grey is Pending with linked work. Jubilee is Pending with no linked work, which is the internal-rule violation.

Hourglass: stalled on us (the only risk-colored glyph, in Jubilee). Envelope: customer gone quiet. Speech bubble with "!": no customer update in 30 days. Broken link: pending with no link, the same meaning as in the Product report. Pause: pending with no reason. Boxed P: linked work is parked. Light bulb: enhancement not routed. Calendar with "!": past due. Check: ready to resolve, in Legacy.
Each ticket lands in exactly one section, the first matching verdict in config order. The healthy section is collapsed by default and opens automatically while a filter is active.
Why "No customer update in 30 days" and not the Timely Updates SLA

The owner chose the relabel on 24 Oct 2026. The check is computed from the newest comment by a team member, because the Timely Updates SLA measures time in Pending: on SUP-1107 its cycle started when the ticket entered Pending, ran through six comments, and stopped only when the status changed.
Why time to resolution isn't a check
It is saturated (breached on most open tickets) and pauses during Pending, so a ticket parked for months never trips it.

The page is 1360px wide and Summary absorbs the remaining width; every other column is fixed. Measured average row height dropped from 92px to 68px at 1280px. Prose is capped at 780px so it stays readable.

Public and internal comments can't be told apart, so an internal note counts as an update. The team roster matches comment authors by display name, because that is all the connector returns. Due dates may be set by automation at intake.
